What is this chapter about?
Teams have a few minutes to review general information about the case. This is a quick orientation chapter, culminating in a short decision where they will reflect on what they expect to happen next.

What to watch for:
  • Do teams move through all of the resources quickly?
Remember to move around to listen to teams' discussions. Sometimes the most insightful comments are said from one participant to another, rather than to an AI character.
Reminder: Move teams to the Decision now.

Decision Time! Teams must state where they anticipate ambiguity or tension might show up as Tanya steps into an elevated role. This is designed to hint toward what comes in future chapters.

Debrief Reminder: This is a quick debrief.
  • Show Approaches in the Debrief tools to show what how teams responded to the reflection question.

What is this chapter about?
Teams must lead a development-focused conversation that helps Tanya to recognize her leadership potential and to see this moment as an opportunity rather than a risk — without pressuring her into saying yes.

What to watch for:
  • Does the team ask what motivates Tanya before presenting the opportunity?
  • Does the team align the development opportunities with Tanya's short- and long-term motivators?
  • Does the team express empathy regarding any apprehension Tanya may feel?
Remember to move around to listen to teams' discussions. Sometimes the most insightful comments are said from one participant to another, rather than to an AI character.

Suggestion: You might consider using the Send Message feature to give participants a helpful reminder:

Remember to ask probing questions to understand what really motivates Tanya!

Chapter 3: Chapter 3 has started.

What is this chapter about?
Teams conduct a performance review with their employee Karl. He's talented and committed, but seeing Tanya take on greater visibility has left him feeling overlooked. The objective is to deliver honest, balanced feedback that acknowledges Karl's strengths while clearly addressing what's holding him back — without losing his trust or engagement.

What to watch for:
  • Does the team acknowledge Karl's strengths before delivering tough feedback?
  • Does the team clearly address business skill gaps (timelines, budget, project management)?
  • Does the team address the new peer-to-supervisor dynamic with Karl constructively?
Remember to move around to listen to teams' discussions. Sometimes the most insightful comments are said from one participant to another, rather than to an AI character.

Suggestion: You might consider using the Send Message feature to give participants a helpful reminder:

Good work so far. Remember to balance encouraging Karl and giving him clear feedback on what he needs to do to improve his skills.

Debrief Reminder: This is a relatively quick debrief.
  • Show Snapshot in the Debrief tools to show how teams performed. If anyone has earned strong team engagement, ask how they achieved that.
  • Use the slides to explore the Do's and Don't's of performance reviews.

Chapter 4: Chapter 4 has started.

What is this chapter about?
An avoidable error has reached a client, exposing cracks in how the team is coordinating. Teams must email the entire team with transparency and purpose: acknowledge recent missteps, reinforce accountability, and restore confidence in the team's ability to deliver.

What to watch for:
  • Does the email acknowledge the specific execution challenges (client error, slipped milestones) transparently?
  • Does the email take accountability without assigning individual blame?
  • Does the email clarify roles, decision rights, and when to escalate to Tanya vs. the manager?
Remember to move around to listen to teams' discussions. Sometimes the most insightful comments are said from one participant to another, rather than to an AI character.
